stories.title: Ukraine backers gather as war escalates
stories.summary: Ukraine will host a meeting of its key European backers today to press for critical air-defence supplies and more pressure on Moscow, with Russian attacks killing more civilians than at any time since the first months of the invasion. The meeting of the Coalition of the Willing will be jointly chaired by the leaders of Britain, France and Germany. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will be in Kyiv for his first international trip since taking office, and several other leaders are expected to join remotely. EU Council President Antonio Costa is also due in Kyiv for the talks, which come amid the latest, deadly escalation of the war.

stories.summary: A 45-year-old man has been charged with the murder of an Irish woman in Melbourne, Australia. She has been named locally as Annmarie O'Reilly, who was from Co Tipperary. Police said emergency services were called to a house on Ferntree Gully Road yesterday morning, where Ms O'Reilly, in her 30s, was found injured. In a statement, police said a man was arrested nearby and taken into custody.

stories.title: Rise in farm payment schemes to tackle fodder shortages
stories.summary: Payments given to farmers under a number of schemes will see an increase from 70% to 75% as part of a plan to alleviate the effects of fodder shortages. The Department of Agriculture has said both the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) and Complementary Redistributive Income Support for Sustainability scheme (CRISS) will see the increase, as well as the Eco Scheme. Minister for Agriculture Martin Heydon said that rules around the Agri-Climate Rural Environment Scheme (ACRES) will also see more flexibility and will now allow for the mowing of almost 26,000 hectares of land from now, rather than from 31 August. "My department administers €1.6 billion worth of payments over the course of the next four months that farmers expect at a certain set time for the different activities that they're carrying out. And I can't do anything to undermine the scheduling of them or to delay in any way those payments," he said.

stories.title: TikTok to pay $400m settlement in children's privacy case
stories.summary: TikTok has agreed to pay $400 million to settle a lawsuit with the US Department of Justice over claims that the video-sharing platform violated federal children's privacy laws, the department has announced. Regulators around the world have been ramping up enforcement against social media companies that violate laws around protecting children's data, privacy and safety. Chinese company ByteDance - which sold off a majority stake of its US entity earlier this year in order to avoid a ban by the Trump administration - is also named as part of the settlement. It has a 19.9% ownership stake in TikTok US, according to US media. "Under the settlement, TikTok will pay $300 million immediately and an additional $100 million upon entry of an order vacating a prior consent decree entered against TikTok's predecessor, Musical.ly," the department said in a statement.

stories.title: Trump to wave green flag for DC indycar street race
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump will cap the celebration of the US 250th anniversary with a first-of-its-kind auto race through the streets of Washington. The event will close a summer defined by sports and spectacle as drivers speed past some of the capital's most iconic landmarks. IndyCar's Freedom 250 Grand Prix will zoom through the National Mall, past the Capitol, down historic Pennsylvania Avenue and around the National Archives. The race is expected to draw roughly 200,000 spectators, officials said, and tickets are free. Passes to private trackside clubs sold for $5,000 (€4,300).

stories.title: UEFA chief Ceferin rules out bid for Infantino's role
stories.summary: UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has ruled himself out of the running to replace FIFA chief Gianni Infantino but warned the beleaguered FIFA chief that he must either quit or face a leadership challenge in March. Infantino has come under increasing pressure to step down over his aborted plans to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, with three continental confederations accusing him of "deception" and UEFA threatening a boycott of FIFA competitions. Despite being widely seen as a potential challenger to Infantino, the 58-year-old Ceferin expressed his commitment to UEFA in an interview with The Rest is Politics podcast. Ceferin said: "I'm not interested because of two reasons. One reason is that I love UEFA and I love working here, and I think that at a certain point… it’s time to also enjoy life a bit.

stories.title: McCartan: Newbies brought 'freshness' to Cork panel
stories.summary: After being in the last six All-Ireland camogie finals and winning three of those, it may have been difficult to change a winning formula. Getting to so many successive finals prove that Cork camogie has clearly been in a golden age. But this season saw a lot of change in the Cork camp. After a very difficult start, forward Sorcha McCartan credited a "freshness" that the new players brought into the senior camogie set up during the season just gone. "I think they brought a bit of a freshness in terms of maybe there was less of a tense atmosphere. Not that the girls that left were tense, but I suppose they were around for so long that they brought a bit of seriousness to it. "They understood the magnitude of trouble that we were in. We had one win on the board at the end of May. That's really unheard of for a Cork camogie team.

stories.title: Russell pleased with Shelbourne's FAI Cup display
stories.summary: Shelbourne booked their place in the Club Orange Women's FAI Cup final in emphatic fashion on Saturday, sweeping aside Cork City with a statement 6-0 victory at Turner's Cross. Seán Russell's side produced a dominant display to secure their place in the decider for the fifth time in six seasons, with their ruthless start setting the tone for a one-sided afternoon in Cork. "We've played Cork twice this year and both times we probably struggled to break them down early on," Russell said. "It was definitely a target that we wanted coming into the game. We wanted to start really fast. We felt like if we did, we could cause some issues and look, we showed that within the first 15 minutes of the game.

stories.title: Munster beat Connacht to extend winning streak to seven
stories.summary: An already-qualified Munster will move on to the Vodafone Women's Interprovincial Championship final in unbeaten form following a 47-12 win away to Connacht. Although Leinster's earlier victory over Ulster ended Connacht's hopes of reaching next week's final at Dexcom Stadium, they put in a gutsy display in their first game in front of the fully-completed Clan Stand. Uillin Eilian had a dream start to her Connacht senior debut, grabbing a third-minute try, but Munster gradually took control of the scoreboard to lead 21-5 at half-time. Alana McInerney's intercept effort was followed by Alisha Flynn driving in under the posts, and then Caitríona Finn's slick 33rd-minute score brought her tally to 11 points.

stories.title: The wild true tale of the syndicate that tried to beat the lotto
stories.summary: What I love about this story is how it illuminates a pivotal moment in Ireland's history in a fascinating and highly entertaining way. Beat The Lotto is a heist film, a caper, a thriller that builds to a very specific climax. In the end, do they win the jackpot or not!? But it’s also about the Irish psyche—how we felt, and still feel, about institutions and taking on the system. Listen: The team behind Beat The Lotto talk to Miriam O'Callaghan The idea for Beat The Lotto first sparked over a decade ago at a friend’s wedding. I found myself sitting beside a guy who worked in big data, which felt relatively new at the time. I asked him if there were any interesting stories in the data world that might make a good documentary. He laughed and said, "No, no! But a story you should look at is that time a syndicate tried to buy all the numbers in the lottery!" Suddenly, I was transported back to 1992. I’d always loved that story. I remembered listening to the radio before school, hearing about a syndicate attempting to buy every possible lottery combination. The sense of intrigue was palpable—a race against time as the lottery scrambled to slow them down.

stories.title: Irish acts showcased on National Public Radio in the US
stories.summary: Irish acts including CMAT, Dermot Kennedy, and Madra Salach will be showcased on National Public Radio (NPR) in the US from Monday as the music programme World Cafe dedicates two weeks to Dublin as part of its award-winning Sense of Place series. From 24 August to 4 September, the nationally syndicated WXPN/Philadelphia programme World Cafe will also feature The Chieftains, Florence Road, Hozier, KhakiKid, Loah, Pillow Queens, the late Sinéad O'Connor, SPRINTS, U2, Riverdance principal dancer Jason O'Neill, and The Ruby Sessions co-founder and booker Conor Donovan in new and archive interviews and performances. "You don't need me to tell you that Dublin has a long, rich history of great storytellers and songwriters," said World Cafe host Raina Douris. "But what moved me most when we recorded these sessions is just how much history is still alive in the newer generation of artists coming up in the city.

stories.title: Nicholas Mosse: Meet the team behind Ireland's favourite ceramics
stories.summary: 50 years in, Ireland’s favourite ceramicists reflect on the importance of handmade art, the fire that nearly ended the business and a new collaboration with JW Anderson. Kate Demolder writes. Even if you don’t know him, you certainly know Nicholas Mosse. Through bowls, mugs and saucers adorned with hand-sponged roses, clovers, or forget-me-nots, the Kilkenny-based potter’s work has evolved from simple household items to beloved monuments of celebration in Irish homes. This is, in part, due to the company’s legacy: this year, the Kilkenny brand boasts a golden anniversary, celebrating 50 years at the epicentre of Irish craft, all while remaining stubbornly, beautifully handmade.

stories.summary: The level of increase in monthly rents slowed in the second quarter of the year, according to a new report from property website Daft. Its Q2 rental report indicates that market rents rose by 1.4% between March and June, which Daft said was "a significant slowdown from the record 4.4% increase in the first quarter and slightly below the average quarterly increase seen over the last decade". It also said rental inflation "remains high in the four major cities outside Dublin". The report shows that market rents in the second quarter were 13% higher year-on-year in Galway city, 12% higher in Cork and up 11% in Limerick.

stories.title: TikTok declines Oireachtas call to discuss driving videos
stories.summary: Social media giant TikTok has declined an invitation to appear before the Oireachtas Committee on Media to discuss the posting of videos of people driving down motorways the wrong way and endangering other people's lives. In a response to a meeting request, a TikTok spokesperson said they cannot attend because of the ongoing garda investigation, a separate examination by Coimisiún na Meán and the fact they are the only company to have been asked to attend. Yesterday, Labour TD and media committee chair Alan Kelly wrote to TikTok requesting that its officials attend a meeting next month to discuss the situation and what he described as "content that glorifies irresponsible or illegal activity". "As a result, we believe it would not be possible to appear before the committee in public session until this process is completed.

stories.title: Wealth Club: Billionaires' big risks buying soccer clubs
stories.summary: The headlines might have implied that we're one step away from seeing the 'Amazon Anfield Arena' but while it is technically the case that Jeff Bezos is buying a stake in Liverpool FC, reality is a little bit more complicated. What is happened is that a consortium called 1892 Holdings has agreed to buy a stake in the club from Fenway Sports Group, which took full control almost 16 years ago. (Initial suggestions were that it would take 30% stake - but later reports indicated it would be closer to a 38% shareholding.) The people behind 1892 Holdings are Amit Bhatia, who is son-in-law of Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, and founder of AyBe Capital Advisers. Bhatai was also, until recently, a co-owner of Queens Park Rangers,but agreed to transfer that stake last month.

stories.summary: Dominik Szoboszlai converted a stoppage-time penalty to snatch a draw as Newcastle and Liverpool served up a Premier League thriller of which Kevin Keegan would have been proud. It was tough on the hosts, who looked to have won it through substitute Joe Willock’s 57th-minute strike just seconds after his introduction in the wake of the Cody Gakpo equaliser which had cancelled out Anthony Elanga’s first-half opener. stories.title: Feely already dreaming of scaling senior heights in 2027
stories.summary: While the achievements of this year are still very fresh in her mind, Roscommon's Aisling Feely is eagerly anticipating the prospect of playing senior championship football in 2027. Courtesy of their emphatic 2-12 to 0-06 triumph over Fermanagh in the TG4 All-Ireland intermediate football championship decider at Croke Park on 2 August, the Rossies will be one of 12 counties to feature in the top-tier of the LGFA next summer. Even before taking part in the race for the Brendan Martin Cup, the primrose and blue will lock horns with newly-crowned All-Ireland senior winners Galway and Mayo in next year’s Connacht championship at the highest grade of ladies football. This will help to make it a three-team series out in the west once again, as it was when the previous season’s All-Ireland intermediate champions Leitrim made the brief step up to senior football in 2025, and Feely is excited about this new opportunity for Roscommon. "We saw Leitrim do it two years ago. We would have been always there or thereabouts with them. They knocked us out in the quarter-final that year by two points and they went on to win it. That gave us a bit of inspiration. If Leitrim can do it, why can’t we. We’re just as good. To get up to senior is absolutely massive," Feely acknowledged.

stories.summary: New Zealand overcame a tough physical challenge to outscore South Africa five tries to one and win the first test 33-16 at Ellis Park on Saturday to go one-up in the four-match series. The All Blacks had been underdogs going into the first international of their eight-match tour but took full advantage of the hosts' numerous handling errors and ill discipline for a statement victory that ended a 12-match winning streak for the Springboks and will rock the confidence of the world champions. Will Jordan extended his run as New Zealand's record try scorer with two tries that bookended scores from Josh Moorby, Fabian Holland and Luke Jacobson. Ruben Love kicked over four conversions. South Africa’s try came from Andre Esterhuizen with three penalties and a conversion from Cheslin Kolbe.

stories.title: Where oh where is our James Connolly? Inside the new documentary
stories.summary: The name of James Connolly has a very special place in the hearts and minds of most Irish people over the generations. Most would remember him for his leadership role in the 1916 Rebellion and his execution, by a British firing squad in Kilmainham Jail, on the 12th of May, 1916. What is often less remembered is that prior to his execution Connolly led an extraordinary life of activism for the labour movement in the UK, USA and Ireland. His wrote many important books and pamphlets and hundreds of articles, songs and speeches. In spite of the greatly changed times we now experience, I believe that Connolly's ideas and philosophy continue to have an enduring relevance for us in today’s unequal world. Before retiring as President of SIPTU in 2003, I agreed with good friends and colleagues in the trade unions (particularly Noírín Greene) that we should cooperate on a project to produce a full-length feature film about Connolly. This was in some respects seen by us as a potentially important contribution for the upcoming 2016 Commemoration of the Rising.

stories.title: Just one in seven public consultants working Saturdays
stories.summary: New figures from the HSE show that just one in seven hospital consultants on the new public-only contracts are working on a Saturday, while just one in three are working extended day shifts. It comes as hospitals prepare for increased pressure over the winter months. The Public Only Consultant Contract was delivered more than three years ago and was designed to make better use of clinics and operating theatres in hospitals. It was also implemented to increase the number of consultants available to treat patients outside Monday to Friday hours.

stories.title: Dáil recall over fuel interventions under review - Burke
stories.summary: An early recall of the Dáil is "under review" by the Government leaders, a Cabinet minister has said, as measures designed to keep fuel costs down are due to be withdrawn. An excise cut of 32c on a litre of diesel and 27c for petrol is due to be phased out from September. The cuts were introduced in April amid major protests that strangled fuel distribution around the country. Today, Minister for Enterprise Peter Burke did not rule out an early return of the Dáil, which is scheduled to resume on 16 September.

stories.title: Judge narrows Ben & Jerry's 'silencing' lawsuit
stories.summary: A United States federal judge has dismissed major portions of a Ben & ⁠Jerry's lawsuit accusing its former parent company Unilever of trying to silence the ice cream maker's social activism, dismantle its board and stop funding its namesake foundation. US District Judge Kevin Castel in Manhattan dismissed seven claims and part of an eighth in a 10-count complaint by Vermont-based Ben & Jerry's and by various independent directors. Judge Castel also said Magnum, the Amsterdam-based company that has owned Ben & Jerry's since it was spun off from Unilever last year, will take Unilever's place as the primary defendant. The dismissed claims relate primarily to how Ben & Jerry's operates, while the two claims that survived in full relate to missed payments by Unilever.

stories.title: McManus: Some county boards view hurling as a 'nuisance'
stories.summary: Former Antrim hurler Neil McManus believes that some county boards regard hurling as a "nuisance" and that counties that ignore the game should be penalised in terms of grants from Croke Park. At the elite level, the 2026 hurling championship was widely viewed as an unsatisfying affair, with an unusually high number of lop-sided games in the Munster championship, culminating in a drab All-Ireland final. While there had been humdrum hurling championships in the past, in 2026 an unflattering light was cast by a newly invigorated football championship, where both the playing rules and the competition format had contributed to one of the most exciting seasons in living memory. Some observers have contended that the commentariat are over-reacting to a single underwhelming campaign but McManus feels the sport has deeper structural issues that need addressing.

stories.title: Kobe-mania and the Irish experiment
stories.summary: The AFL's Irish experiment nearly failed before even it really even began - and it all came down to a split-second decision in the 1987 Victorian Football League preliminary final between Melbourne and Hawthorn. The VFL was three years from morphing into the AFL and a huge crowd had gathered to watch what turned into a manic final quarter with tennis legend Pat Cash even interrupting a family holiday to attend. Melbourne missed chance after chance to kill off the Hawks’ challenge in the final minutes of the match, Simon Eishold’s incredible mis-hit hook behind long remembered by Demons fans, but it was the final play that saw it go down in infamy and left recently-recruited Dubliner Jim Stynes labelled as a laughing stock. Kept alive by Melbourne’s inefficiency, Gary Buckenara was given one last chance to win it from Hawthorn but from way out, it was a low percentage chance.
